scenes.why: The turn: the product the guide itself hands over to, named and shown on its real screen, captioned with its listing's line closest to what the guide teaches. Screen: "Lisbon and Porto" (The trip: where you are now, destinations, and every booking with its reference, with Record a change on each.) chosen because it is the real screen closest to "Record the change and it walks down everything you said was booked around it, on"; focus on "Flight to Lisbon".
Ends on where to read the whole guide, with the product beneath it: the viewer leaves with the next step, not only a pitch.

reasoning.decision: Transitions follow the product's own identity motif, "timeline"
reasoning.because: Transitions follow the product's own identity motif, "timeline": a trip is a line through time, so scenes travel left to right along it.
Camera "dolly": constant forward movement for a high-energy feed.
Grounds light → light → ink → accent: a cool accent, so a darker ground is used for contrast at a turn.
Sound-on placement: every transition, landing and reveal has a cue, and the bed ducks under the brand moment.
Each scene is held for the time its words take to read on YouTube Short (0.26s a word), inside 18–45s.
